segments.say: Lesson 16. Multi-Agent Systems & M C P. Supervisor, hierarchical, swarm/handoff patterns, plus the Model Context Protocol for plugging tools into any agent.

Multi-agent systems split a big task across specialist agents coordinated by a supervisor. M C P (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for plugging tools and data into any A I app the same way. Here is an analogy. A hospital: a coordinator routes the patient to the right specialists and combines their findings. M C P is like a universal plug socket, so any device fits any outlet.

Why does this matter? Common in enterprise agent design discussions. M C P is quickly becoming the standard way to give agents tools. A few key words. Supervisor: Agent that delegates and merges results. Handoff: One agent passing control to another. M C P server: Wraps a system (GitHub, a D B) and exposes its tools. M C P client: Lives in the A I app and calls M C P servers.
Supervisor pattern. A complex task needs different expertise and tools.
A supervisor L L M breaks it down and decides which specialist to call next.
Each specialist agent has a focused prompt and a small toolset, so tool selection gets better and context stays clean.
Specialists report back. The supervisor correlates: "deploy at 14:02 leads to error logs at 14:03 leads to p99 latency up".
Final synthesized answer. In Lang Graph each specialist is a subgraph and the supervisor routes with conditional edges or handoff Command s.

segments.say: An M C P server wraps a system and exposes tools (actions), resources (readable data) and prompts (templates).

segments.say: Any M C P client (Claude, I D Es, Lang Graph via adapters) discovers and calls them the same way: N plus M instead of N times M.

segments.say: Transports: stdio for local servers, streamable H T T P for remote ones, with auth (OAuth). Security: only connect trusted servers, since tool descriptions and outputs can carry prompt injection.

Multi-agent patterns. Supervisor: a central router agent delegates to specialists. Hierarchical: supervisors of supervisors, for big organizations of agents. Network / swarm (handoffs): agents hand control directly to each other. Orchestrator-workers: a planner spawns parallel workers for subtasks and merges the results. Debate / critic: one agent proposes, another reviews.

When multi-agent is worth it. Distinct domains with different tools and prompts, parallelizable research, context too big for one agent. Simple tasks: multi-agent multiplies tokens, latency and coordination failures. Often one agent with good tools wins.
A2A versus M C P. M C P connects an agent to tools and data. Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocols connect agents to other agents across vendors (agent cards, task delegation). They complement each other.

Say it in the interview. "I'd use a supervisor pattern when sub-domains need different tools, for example logs, metrics and deploys for incident R C A, each as a Lang Graph subgraph with a narrow toolset. Tools are exposed via M C P servers, so the same Splunk or GitHub integration works in Claude, our I D E and our agents. I'd only go multi-agent where evals show it beats a single well-equipped agent, since it multiplies cost and latency.".

Let's compare. Single agent plus tools: one loop, most tasks, tool overload if too many. Supervisor: central router, clear specialist domains, supervisor bottleneck. Hierarchical: tree of supervisors, very large systems, latency, complexity. Swarm / handoff: peer-to-peer, conversational routing (sales leads to support), loops, lost context. Orchestrator-workers: planner plus parallel workers, research, big code changes, merge quality.
M C P primitives. Tools: model (it decides to call), create issue, run query. Resources: application (it attaches data), file contents, D B schema. Prompts: user (picks a template), "/summarize-pr".

A likely interview question: What is M C P and why does it matter? A strong answer: An open protocol for connecting L L M apps to tools, data and prompts through servers. Write an integration once and use it from any M C P-capable client. That cuts glue code from N times M to N+M.
That's it for Multi-Agent Systems & M C P. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
